text: Everything covered so far in this chapter assumes there's a record, and a form built from that record, driving the interaction. Sometimes that assumption doesn't hold, and that's the gap a UI Page exists to fill.

A UI Page, stored on sys_ui_page, is a standalone custom page with its own URL. Think of a multi-step wizard that walks a user through choices before any record even exists, a summary dashboard pulling from several tables with no single current record, or the contents of a popup dialog triggered by a button. None of those map cleanly onto a table's form.

A UI Page's HTML field is written in Jelly, an XML-based templating language that predates most of the modern platform. g colon tags are ServiceNow's own custom tags, j colon tags are Jelly's core control flow. Here, g:evaluate runs a server-side script expression at render time and stores the result in jvar_count - that jvar underscore prefix is a strict Jelly naming convention, not optional. j:if then checks that variable server-side, before any HTML reaches the browser.

A UI Page isn't limited to server-side Jelly, though. Its HTML field can also hold a plain script block that runs exactly like JavaScript on any other web page. This example defines a refreshSummary function that updates a span's text using the DOM the Jelly just rendered - Jelly builds the page server-side, and ordinary JavaScript takes over once that HTML is sitting in the browser.

Here's the honest context worth carrying forward: Jelly and UI Pages predate almost everything else in this course, and UI Builder - the modern, component-based page builder from Course 2 - is the better tool for most new custom-interface work today. Jelly's XML syntax is verbose and its debugging story is weaker than modern JavaScript tooling.

UI Pages still matter, though, because an enormous amount of existing platform functionality and customer customization was built on them over nearly two decades. One specific, still-current use case worth flagging now: a UI Page is exactly what you point a GlideDialogWindow at to supply the custom body of a popup dialog - a mechanism Chapter 7 covers in depth. Next lesson is this chapter's lab - a full worked scenario combining a server-side UI Action and a scripted UI Policy on a real Problem record.
